notes: Catalysis paper (chlorobenzene hydrodechlorination over Pd and Ni). The only H2 uptake values are pulse H2 chemisorption volumes (Table 1, 'H2 uptake (cm3/g)', e.g. Pd/AC 1.0, Ni/AC 3.8) measured in a flow (CHEMBET 3000, TCD) to obtain metal surface area; I1 is judged met on the literal criterion (gas-phase H2 uptake by a flow method) and I2 by the ~8 wt% metal on activated carbon, graphite and GNF supports. The other hydrogen data are TPD release amounts, TPR and the HDC reaction, none of which is an uptake value. I3 fails: the chemisorption temperature is given only in words ('room temperature'; p. 5: 'Pulse hydrogen chemisorption (under ambient conditions)'), which the data dictionary treats as not stated numerically, and the only pressure is the maximum H2 partial pressure of a pulse (0.004 atm), not the pressure of the cumulative uptake. If I1 were instead judged not met (chemisorption for metal dispersion rather than sorption uptake), the code would still be no_conditions_stated. Not a review; record is_retracted false and no retraction statement; no statement that all uptake values were published before (only that Pd/GNF and Pd/graphite HDC was first reported in ref. [37]).
